title: Go SDK: resumable streams with per-message deadlines and in-flight buffering
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a Go SDK streaming API that supports per-message deadlines, deterministic in-flight buffering, and resumable client-driven reconnects so applications can handle partial responses, intermittent networking, and bounded wait semantics without duplicating server-side work.

Background: Current streaming primitives expose a single overall context/deadline for the lifetime of the stream. In practice many Redwood users need finer-grained control: short deadlines for individual messages (e.g., token generation timeouts), long-lived meta-sessions, and the ability to reconnect and resume from a checkpoint when connections drop. Existing tickets around cancellation and deadline propagation focused on top-level semantics; this work designs an ergonomic API for per-message timeouts + buffered ack/resume checkpoints while preserving correctness with server-side idempotency and retry policies.

Success criteria:
- Provide a Go API that lets callers specify a per-message timeout while keeping a parent ctx for connection lifetime.
- Implement a small bounded in-memory buffer for recently-sent messages and received partial frames to support reconnection resume without replaying entire request bodies.
- Add wire-level checkpoint framing (client-side) compatible with server resume paths (server changes tracked separately).
- Ensure behavior is deterministic under cancellation, partial-EOF, and reconnects (no silent duplication of final tokens).
- Backwards compatible: existing simple streaming calls keep previous ergonomics.

Design highlights and trade-offs:
- API shape: StreamingSession{ctx, Open(), Send(ctxPerMessage,...), Recv(ctxPerMessage)} where Send/Recv accept per-message contexts that derive from the session ctx. This keeps the parent lifetime and supports tight per-message deadlines.
- Buffering: bounded ring buffer (configurable, default 64 messages) holds recent outbound frames and inbound partial results for replay on resume. Trade-off: memory vs resume fidelity. Default chosen for common mobile/edge cases.
- Resume semantics: on reconnect the client offers the last offset/checkpoint; server verifies and resumes emitting remaining frames. If server does not support resume, client falls back to full retry with de-duplication heuristics and logs.
- Idempotency: to minimize server changes we add lightweight client-generated message IDs (UUID v4) used for de-duplication and matching acknowledgements without requiring strong transactional semantics.
- Deadlines vs retries: per-message deadlines cancel only that Send/Recv call; the session remains open for subsequent messages. Retries for ephemeral network errors respect message IDs to avoid duplicate processing.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) API proposal + acceptance tests (unit + integration): create proposal PR + mock server harness that simulates mid-stream disconnects.
2) Implement ring buffer + message ID envelope in SDK, wire framing helpers.
3) Integrate per-message ctx into existing streaming internals (reader/writer loops), ensure no regression for existing clients.
4) Add reconnection path: negotiate resume with server, replay necessary frames from buffer.
5) Add end-to-end tests: flaky networking harness, perf microbench, memory regression.
6) Docs + code samples (Go examples showing per-message timeout and graceful reconnect).

Testing and telemetry:
- Unit tests for timeout cancellation semantics (verify parent ctx unaffected).
- Integration tests with a test server that supports/doesn't support resume to validate fallback behavior.
- Stress tests with high message rate to validate bounded buffer prevents OOM.
- Add telemetry counters: resume_attempts, resume_success, per_message_timeout_count, buffer_overflow_count.

Rollout strategy:
- Feature flag behind runtime config for early dogfood users.
- Beta in SDK-release channel; collect feedback.
- Docs migration note for teams that rely on single ctx semantics.

Open questions / risks:
- Server-side resume protocol needs design iteration (tracked in separate server ticket).
- How to handle large message bodies in the buffer (stream vs chunked storage)? For now limit to message headers + pointers to ephemeral file-backed storage in extreme cases.
- Interaction with existing batching and KV cache: ensure resume does not violate cache assumptions.
